summary: Built and rendered the first full production GPU/AI explainer video (2:52) on the TASK-010 scene engine, using the project's existing content/gpu_story.txt and content/gpu_story_scenes.json (9-scene structure, ~165s target) as the source of truth rather than inventing new claims -- adapted into per-scene narration segments in content/gpu_explainer_script.json. This closes the TASK-010 architectural gap: each of the 9 scenes (Hook, Why GPUs Matter, CPU vs GPU, Massive Parallelism, Memory + Bandwidth, GPU Clusters, Serving Millions of Requests, The Real Cost, Takeaway) synthesizes its own narration clip, and the whole video's timeline is derived from those 9 measured clip durations, not a hand-picked duration. The combined audio track uses ffmpeg adelay+amix (normalize disabled since clips never overlap) to place each clip at its scene's exact narration start time. 6 of the 9 scene diagrams reuse TASK-009's helpers (core_grid, hand_connector, Camera) directly; the other 3 (AI Model compute-heavy grid, GPU<->memory bandwidth flow, many-users-to-cluster inference visual) are new content built from the same primitives -- no new rendering engine code. Per TASK-011's explicit instruction, also tuned scene_engine.transition_sweep() (the TASK-010 regression review had flagged it as too dominant): half_width 0.35->0.18, strength 0.10->0.045; verified subtle on an actual scene boundary in the final render rather than assumed. All 4 canonical character poses (introg, explaining, thinking, closing) are used across the 9 scenes with appropriate variety; the 'reference' pose remains excluded per the known TASK-008/009 limitation.
